observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: A dark-green fern clump on transparent alpha. About ten pinnate fronds grow from a tight base low on the left of centre. Almost every frond arcs up and then sweeps hard to the right, so the plant is strongly one-sided. Each frond has a pale cream-green midrib that stands out against the dark leaflets. Three or four young fronds on the left are still curled at the tip like fiddleheads. The paint is fine and detailed, close to a botanical illustration, with soft shading and no drawn black keyline. There is no soil, rock or shadow under it. The base sits at the bottom edge of the canvas, and the plant fills most of the frame.

Max zoom: the fern stands in one cell beside the vanilla human and comes up to about the human's chest or shoulder. Its rightward sweep and pale midribs are clear. At 32 px per cell it reads as a dark-green fern tuft, darker than the ground, and the one-sided lean still shows. At 18 px per cell it is a small dark-green tuft.

Its face and belly are white, its back and stub wings are mottled grey-brown, and it has orange-tan patches around huge black eyes, orange legs and webbed feet. South is noticeably shorter and narrower than east and north: the body is smaller overall, not just a different pose.
observed.south.png: A front view. The face points at the camera: two large glossy black eyes ringed in orange-tan, a tiny nostril bump and a small downturned mouth line, and no beak. The breast is fluffy white, the stub wings are folded at the sides, and the orange webbed feet stand below. Painterly feather texture, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. One large black eye with an orange-tan ring, a flat beakless face with a slight bump, a big white round belly, and a folded mottled grey-brown wing along the flank. Orange legs and webbed feet show below the belly. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view: a rounded back of layered grey-brown feathers with a warm tan wash at the crown. Both wings are folded, a little white shows at the lower flanks, and the orange feet are visible. No face, no eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the porg is about the height of the human's head-and-torso block, a small bird. At 32 px per cell it reads as a white-and-brown roundish shape with a dark eye dot, smaller than the human and larger than the rat.

South wing layers: brown wing arches with white belly fluff on their inner and lower edges, also cut with a straight vertical inner edge. East plate: the head and belly with a large empty hole in the back and flank where the wing was cut out, plus a thin brown arc of back at the left. East wing layer: the folded wing with a flat, unpainted grey-taupe fill at its lower right. North plate: a narrow straight-sided brown column. North wing layers: brown wings with white flank pixels at their bottom edges and straight inner edges.

observed.flight_2.png: East f2. Almost the same as f1. The flat grey patch is still visible under the wing.
observed.flight_3.png: East f3. The wing has rotated down toward the body and the grey patch is mostly hidden. Head is fixed.
observed.flight_4.png: East f4. The wing hangs lower. A few detached dark feather specks float at the far left edge, near x≈82, y≈175.
observed.flight_5.png: East f5. Like f4: the wing is down and the stray specks at the left edge are still there.
observed.flight_6.png: East f6. Same as f4 and f5, stray specks included.

observed.flight_9.png: North f1. Both wings are spread out to the sides. The body between them is a narrow column with straight vertical sides, and white flank pixels hang from the wing undersides.
observed.flight_10.png: North f2. Like f1: the wings are spread and the body is a straight-sided column.
observed.flight_11.png: North f3. The wings are half lowered. Ragged white fringes trail at the bottom edges of both wings, where flank pixels went with them.
observed.flight_12.png: North f4. The wings are nearly folded and the body looks almost whole.
observed.flight_13.png: North f5. The wings are folded; it looks close to the grounded rear view.
